title: [Bug] direct_compile reuses executables for scalar views with incompatible backing layouts
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no existing report for this failure mode.
- [x] The relevant shape-only compatibility behavior is present on the latest public main branch.
- [x] A minimal reproducible demo is included below.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

## Describe the bug

`direct_compile` can reuse a cached executable for two scalar tensor inputs whose logical shapes are both `()`, even when their physical backing layouts are incompatible.

A concrete case is an indexed scalar view such as:

```python
active_num_tokens = cu_q_lens[non_empty_bs]
```

TorchTPU reconstructs a view by passing the minimum contiguous base buffer required by its storage offset. Therefore:

- a scalar view at offset 128 is represented by a physical `s32[129]` parameter;
- a scalar view at offset 125 is represented by a physical `s32[126]` parameter.

The current `direct_compile` runtime guard checks the Python tensor type and logical shape, so both inputs appear compatible. Reusing the executable compiled at offset 128 with the view at offset 125 reaches XLA and fails with:

```text
RuntimeProgramInputMismatch:
Executable(tt_jit_add) expected parameter 0 of size 1024 (s32[129]{0:T(256)})
but got buffer with incompatible size 512 (s32[126]{0:T(128)})
```

This is not specific to one attention field. Any future scalar view passed to `direct_compile` can encounter the same problem when its storage offset changes while its logical shape stays scalar.

## Reproduction

It was discovered during an integration test that warmed up the Pallas RPA decode path with 128 active batch slots, then reused the same direct-compiled artifact after request retraction reduced the active width to 125.

This minimal compiler-only reproduction does not require a model or SGLang attention setup:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import torch
import torch_tpu  # noqa: F401 -- registers the TPU backend
from torch_tpu._internal import execution_mode
from torch_tpu._internal.compile import tpu_torch_compile


def scalar_view(offset: int):
    base = torch.arange(129, dtype=torch.int32, device="tpu")
    return base, base[offset]


compile_base, compile_scalar = scalar_view(128)
graph_input = tpu_torch_compile.placeholder_like(compile_scalar)

with execution_mode.set_eager_mode(
    execution_mode.EagerMode.INTERNAL_DEFER_ALL
):
    graph_output = graph_input + graph_input

executable = tpu_torch_compile.traverse_and_compile(
    [graph_output], [graph_input]
).executable

warm_output = tpu_torch_compile.execute(executable, [compile_scalar])
print("warmup:", warm_output[0].cpu().item(), flush=True)

runtime_base, runtime_scalar = scalar_view(125)
print(
    "runtime input:",
    {
        "base_shape": tuple(runtime_base.shape),
        "scalar_shape": tuple(runtime_scalar.shape),
        "scalar_storage_offset": runtime_scalar.storage_offset(),
    },
    flush=True,
)

failing_output = tpu_torch_compile.execute(executable, [runtime_scalar])
print("unexpected success:", failing_output[0].cpu().item(), flush=True)
```

Observed output:

```text
warmup: 256
runtime input: {'base_shape': (129,), 'scalar_shape': (), 'scalar_storage_offset': 125}
RuntimeProgramInputMismatch:
Executable(tt_jit_add) expected parameter 0 of size 1024 (s32[129]{0:T(256)})
but got buffer with incompatible size 512 (s32[126]{0:T(128)})
```

## Possible fixes:
PR [#559](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/559) is the immediate unblocker, but doesn't fix it systematically.

PR [#566](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/566) fixes the problem systematically at the `direct_compile` boundary. It materializes every explicit scalar view into owned scalar storage during both tracing and runtime execution, so future callers cannot accidentally create an offset-dependent executable input shape. It leaves owned scalars, non-scalar views, model state, and mutable KV-pool inputs unchanged.


## Environment

- Accelerator: TPU v7
- Reproduction date: 2026-08-28
- Relevant current public sources:
  - [sglang-torchtpu `direct_compile.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/5df2a212b420dce058491fcf90f3b0a1ffaa3238/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/compilation/direct_compile.py)
  - [TorchTPU placeholder construction](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/blob/abd45952c2d54ba4a4e6d1a6b4e7814cd395ab24/torch_tpu/_internal/compile/tpu_torch_compile.cc)
  - [TorchTPU compiled argument preparation](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/blob/abd45952c2d54ba4a4e6d1a6b4e7814cd395ab24/torch_tpu/_internal/compile/compiled_mode.cc)

title: [Bug] GPT-OSS cache oracle regressed after TorchTPU TopK tie-order change
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and did not find one tracking this exact GPT-OSS regression.
- [x] The failure reproduces in public CI with fixed SGLang, Raiden, LibTPU, and PyTorch versions.
- [x] Published-wheel, source-commit, and causal-revert results are linked below.

## TL;DR

[TorchTPU PR #2883](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/pull/2883) changed `torch.topk` from an explicitly unstable StableHLO sort-and-slice lowering to a CHLO TopK builder call whose omitted `is_stable` argument defaults to `true`. That tie-order change causes the GPT-OSS prefix-cache/KV-offload text oracle to fail. Restoring only `is_stable=false` while retaining the new CHLO implementation makes the full test pass again.

The evidence does not indicate physical KV-cache corruption. Cache accounting remains exact, device-cache and host-reload requests return the same text, general GSM8K accuracy remains healthy, and changing only MoE TopK tie ordering restores the test without touching cache code.

## Details

The failure was caught by the single-host GPT-OSS 120B prefix-cache/KV-offload test added in [sglang-torchtpu PR #492](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/492). The test sends the same forced-counting prompt three times: a cold request, an immediate device-cache hit, and a request after the prefix has been evicted to and reloaded from host.

In the failing configuration, cache accounting is correct:

```text
cold:        (0, 0)       device/host cached tokens
device hit:  (1984, 0)    device/host cached tokens
host reload: (0, 1984)    device/host cached tokens
```

The cold request passes the counting predicate, while the device-cache and host-reload requests both return the same rejected continuation beginning with `13` and explaining that the next number is 13. The same server passes the 200-example GSM8K check around `0.85`, above its `0.70` floor.

## Bisection

All meaningful boundary runs use the same sglang-torchtpu source base, Raiden `0.0.1.dev20260819190323`, LibTPU `0.0.44.1`, PyTorch `2.11.0`, original model recipe, cache settings, prompt, and assertions.

### Published wheels

- Last good: `torch-tpu==0.1.1.dev20260818130139`.
- First bad: `torch-tpu==0.1.1.dev20260818211054`.
- Both use `INTERNAL_DEFER_ALL`, so `INTERNAL_COMPILE_FX_GRAPH` is not causal.
- The bundled XLA runtime is identical across the boundary, ruling out the preceding XLA roll.

The full wheel history and public jobs are recorded in diagnostic [PR #551](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/551).

### Source commits

| TorchTPU source snapshot | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Through [`4fb6416a`](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/commit/4fb6416a477fb30a94d5617fc5326864332590ac), immediately before the TopK rewrite | Pass: cold `(0, 0)`, device `(1984, 0)`, host `(0, 1984)`; GSM8K `0.805` | [Job #98807796145](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/actions/runs/33157275077/job/98807796145) |
| Through [`cd593b97`](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/commit/cd593b97a443eb7c6ab23b60ba16acfe2f0e9f60), with no later runtime commit | Fail: both cached reads produce the same rejected continuation; cache counts remain correct; GSM8K `0.850` | [Job #98821023065](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/actions/runs/33161326737/job/98821023065) |

This identifies [`cd593b97`](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/commit/cd593b97a443eb7c6ab23b60ba16acfe2f0e9f60), from [TorchTPU PR #2883](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/pull/2883), as the first offending commit. No later compiler or event-queue change is required.

## Root cause and causal confirmation

Before `cd593b97`, TorchTPU explicitly passed `is_stable=false` to `stablehlo.sort`. After the change, it calls `chlo::TopK` without a stability argument. At the [exact StableHLO revision pinned by that TorchTPU source](https://github.com/openxla/stablehlo/blob/7b1b15781ccbd770f50c7eef4b0c3e03834649fd/docs/generated/ChloBuilder.md#chlotopkop), the builder default is `is_stable=true`. The tests added by PR #2883 skip index comparison when values are tied, so they did not detect this semantic change.

GPT-OSS uses `torch.topk` in every sparse-MoE layer to select experts. Its BF16 router scores can tie, and PyTorch does not guarantee which indices are returned for tied values. Changing the tie policy can therefore change the generated continuation, particularly between long cold-prefill and short cached-prefill graph shapes, without corrupting stored KV tensors.

[Diagnostic PR #555](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/555) retains the new CHLO TopK implementation and changes only the builder argument to `is_stable=false`, matching the old lowering. The focused test [passes in job #98823529001](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/actions/runs/33162545214/job/98823529001):

```text
cold:        (0, 0)
device hit:  (1984, 0)
host reload: (0, 1984)
prefix-cache/KV-offload gate: PASS
GSM8K: 0.855
overall: PASS
```

This controlled result confirms that the implicit unstable-to-stable TopK tie-selection change caused the observed test regression.

## Recommended follow-up

1. In TorchTPU, pass `is_stable=false` explicitly to `chlo::TopK` to preserve the pre-#2883 behavior.
2. Add a TopK regression test with duplicate values so a tie-order semantic change cannot be hidden by skipping index comparison.
3. Strengthen the sglang-torchtpu cache test so a non-counting model continuation is not described as proof of physical KV corruption. A data-plane assertion should distinguish stored/reloaded tensor mismatches from allowed model-output variation.

[Issue #321](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/issues/321) is related background: it documents cold-versus-prefix-cache greedy-output variation on TPU even without host KV offload.

## Environment

- Hardware: single-host TPU v7, TP8 and EP8
- Model: GPT-OSS 120B
- Python: 3.12
- Attention backend: `pallas_tpu_rpa_v3`
- KV cache dtype: `fp8_e4m3`
- Device cache: radix cache enabled, 64-token pages
- Original full test: Raiden-backed HiCache, `page_first_fused`, `write_through`
- SGLang-TorchTPU source base: [`d751d467a2`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/commit/d751d467a2)
- Raiden: `0.0.1.dev20260819190323`
- LibTPU: `0.0.44.1`
- PyTorch: `2.11.0`

title: Restructure raiden/conn.py per-room state into a rooms: dict[int, RoomState] abstraction
body:
From the #460 review (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/460#discussion_r3863794325):

> would it make sense (not in this PR) to refactor raiden/conn.py to have a `rooms: dict[int, PullRoomState | ReshardRoomState]` abstraction? right now It's difficult to tell what state is for which one (the symmetric case or the asymmetric case)

`RaidenKVManager` keeps roughly forty flat per-room dicts and sets. Problems:

- Which table serves which path (symmetric pull, asymmetric reshard, or both) is convention only; classifying a table requires reading call sites.
- Cleanup must sweep every table individually, and a missed table is invisible until it leaks. Several bugs fixed in #460 were this class.
- The prefill and decode modes install disjoint attribute sets on the same class, so wrong-mode access fails only at runtime.

General direction (concrete design up to the assignee): one state object per room, so cleanup drops a single entry; make the pull-only, reshard-only, and shared-by-both state explicit; and keep per-transfer records inside each room -- a room's closing read, sliding-window read, and chunk transfers settle independently, which today is tracked in parallel completion/failure sets.

Related, if the call sites are being touched anyway: unify the `check_status` contract for a missing room (the common base and raiden raise `KeyError`, NIXL returns `WaitingForInput`; shared callers currently defend against both -- see https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/pull/460#discussion_r3863308083).

---

Appendix -- current per-room state by path, from `RaidenKVManager.__init__` at [451483ca10](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/451483ca10/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/conn.py#L200-L310):

|---|---|---|

| **Shared by both paths** | `_send_blocks`, `_send_swa_blocks`, `_send_aux` (both `BLOCKS` and `RESHARD_BLOCKS` announce from these), `_send_total`, `_pending_offer`, `_chunk_seq` | -- |

Both sides, both paths (the shared core): `request_status`, `failure_records` (from `CommonKVManager`), `_aborted` (tombstone), `_failed` (logical room failure), `_completed_send`, `_completed_recv`, `_native_failed` (per-transfer engine settlement), `_reshard_slot_of` (reshard-only, room -> staging slot).

Per-manager rather than per-room (stays off the room object): `_pulling` (slot admission), `_reshard_slot_rooms` (staging slot pool), the locks, `_push_executor`.

body:
### Checklist

### Bug

TPU fused reduce-scatter MoE can deadlock during EAGLE3 speculative-decoding startup on a large FP8 MoE model.

The observed failure uses Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8 on one TPU v7x host with TP8/EP8. During speculative graph warmup, all ranks stall while materializing `EXTEND(FULL)` at `tokens=2048, bs=16`:

```text
torch.tpu.synchronize()
  -> decoder_compile_policy._materialize_out()
  -> _precompile_extend()
  -> spec_decode_compile_policy.precompile()
```

The target MoE path is using `pallas_tpu_fused_rs` while EAGLE3 adds its auxiliary-hidden-state collective to the same compiled graph. The server never becomes healthy and remains stuck until the outer CI timeout.

### Reproduction

Immutable failing run:

- Run: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/actions/runs/32813014563/job/97699732406
- Source SHA: `9e468c882b55efafce16762f3a81e4353574b336`
- Test: `test/registered/tpu/e2e/test_tpu_qwen3_coder_480b_singlehost_spec_decoding_gsm8k.py`

Configuration:

```text
target: /weights/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8
draft: /weights/SGLang-EAGLE3-Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-SpecForge-EigenAI
topology: single-host TPU v7x, TP8, EP8
attention: pallas_tpu_rpa_v3
target MoE runner: pallas_tpu_fused_rs
EAGLE3: steps=3, topk=1, draft_tokens=4
tpu_compile_tokens: 512 2048 4096
tpu_compile_bs: 1 2 4 16
context_length: 8192
max_total_tokens: 8192
```

On a revision containing the current automatic fallback, force the affected path with:

```text
--moe-runner-backend pallas_tpu_fused_rs
```

and otherwise use the launch environment from the test above.

### Expected behavior

The fused-RS MoE path should compile and serve EAGLE3 requests successfully. If the combination is unsupported, startup should fail promptly with an actionable error rather than hanging indefinitely.

### Actual behavior

Speculative `EXTEND(FULL)` materialization deadlocks at `torch.tpu.synchronize()` and the server never reports healthy.

### Controls and current containment

- Selecting the explicit non-fused `pallas_tpu` MoE runner avoids the deadlock.
- Non-speculative serving can continue to select `pallas_tpu_fused_rs` automatically.
- #456 introduced the containment: speculative decoding on TPU resolves `moe_runner_backend=auto` to `pallas_tpu`.
- #499 restores that containment after it was lost during an upstream sync.
- Dense Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B EAGLE3 tests do not exercise this kernel and therefore cannot detect the runtime failure.

Related work:

- #456
- #499
- #308 (related fused-RS work, but a different failure mode)

### Environment

- Google TPU v7x, single host
- TP8 / EP8
- FP8 target MoE
- `torch.compile` enabled
- `pallas_tpu_rpa_v3` attention
- Exact container and dependency versions are preserved in the linked CI run.

body:
`test_tpu_gpt_oss_120b.py` has failed at compile on every nightly since at least 2026-08-16, blocking the `nightly-tpu-4-v7` suite.

```
RuntimeError: Failed to traverse and compile: failed to get fixed shape kernel:
failed to compile MLIR module -- the XLA compiler failed with: ran out of memory on HBM,
the total memory required for HLO temporaries (142.23G) exceeds available HBM (94.74G)
```

Dies while compiling **EXTEND/MIXED at batch_size=32** on one v7x host. Deterministic — same 142.23G on every run.

The test docstring records this exact config green on 2026-08-04, so it is a regression.

### Ruled out: direct_compile (#351)

#351 added `--tpu-compile-tracer direct` to `recipe/gpt_oss_120b/server.sh` on 08-12, which looked like the cause since the traceback ran through `direct_compile.py`. Tested by commenting that line out ([run 32099081147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/actions/runs/32099081147)):

- `direct_compile.py` confirmed gone from the traceback, so the old path really was used
- **still fails with the identical 142.23G**

Byte-identical across both compile paths means the demand comes from the shape being compiled, not from how it is traced.

### Where to look next

Whatever sets the extend/prefill shape for this model between 08-04 and 08-12 — the bucket grid and `MEM_FRACTION_STATIC=0.6` in `recipe/gpt_oss_120b/server.sh`, or a graph change in the model/attention path.

Cheapest next probe: drop `batch_size=32` from the extend grid. Compiling at a smaller extend shape would localise this to bucket sizing rather than a code regression.

### Notes

- `test_tpu_nightly_smoke.py` in the same suite passes.
- Nightlies before 08-14 are all `cancelled` (the pre-#316 concurrency-drop bug), so there is no clean first-failure to bisect against.

- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

With Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8 on one 8-chip TPU v7x host, identical greedy requests can produce slightly different text across two DP replicas. The observed difference is punctuation-level and has occurred both during explicitly routed cold priming and after cache reuse. This reproduces in feature combo2, where speculative decoding is disabled and the KV cache is BF16. The model weights remain FP8, so this is not an FP8-KV-only or cache-only issue; rank-dependent FP8 weight execution is the leading hypothesis, but the root cause is not yet proven.

- Identical `temperature=0` requests are not guaranteed to return identical text across DP replicas.
- Exact-output correctness checks become flaky depending on DP routing, even when both requests are cold.
- A punctuation-only difference can still change subsequent autoregressive tokens for longer generations.

### Reproduction

Run combo2 with the 480B profile on an 8-chip TPU host:

```bash
SGLANG_PLATFORM=tpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
MODEL=/models/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8 \
python3 test/manual/tpu/feature_combo/test_feature_combos_singlehost.py \
  --model-profile qwen3-coder-480b 2 \
  TestFeatureCombo.test_2_shared_prefix_questions
```

For a precise rank/cache-state reproduction, flush the engine cache once, then issue the same prompt three times to each DP replica using `routed_dp_rank` and record the requested rank, returned `meta_info.dp_rank`, `cached_tokens`, and output:

```python
engine.flush_cache()
for repeat in range(3):
    for rank in range(2):
        out = engine.generate(
            prompt,
            {"temperature": 0.0, "max_new_tokens": 12},
            routed_dp_rank=rank,
        )
        print(repeat, rank, out["meta_info"], repr(out["text"]))
```

## Observed behavior

Some runs diverged during one-request-per-rank cold priming: both requests were explicitly routed to different DP replicas and reported `cached_tokens=0`, but returned different greedy text.

- Hardware: single TPU v7x host, topology `2x2x1`, 8 chips
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct-FP8`
- Weight quantization: FP8, `tpu_fp8_runtime=channelwise`

The test first primes both DP workers with greedy requests, evicts the cached
prefix, and then submits one concurrent batch. The final batch contains 16
prompts and requests 12 new tokens per prompt.



### Reproduction

## Reproduce

Use a timeout so the hung workers are eventually stopped. The timeout includes
model loading and compilation, so increase it if compilation takes longer on
the test host.

Default behavior, with token-ID synchronization disabled:

```bash
timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=30s 900s \
  env -u SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP \
  SGLANG_PLATFORM=tpu \
  MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B \
  python test/manual/tpu/feature_combo/test_feature_combos_singlehost.py \
  2 TestFeatureCombo.test_5_concurrent_churn
```

The environment variable does not work around the problem:

```bash
timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=30s 900s \
  env SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=1 \
  SGLANG_PLATFORM=tpu \
  MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B \
  python test/manual/tpu/feature_combo/test_feature_combos_singlehost.py \
  2 TestFeatureCombo.test_5_concurrent_churn
```

## Observed results

Both variants were validated on 2026-08-11 with commit `fe5439037` and a
600-second timeout.

| `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` | Compile time | Time in test before timeout | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| unset | 253.5 seconds | about 5 minutes | timed out |
| `1` | 248.8 seconds | about 5 minutes | timed out |

In both runs, model loading and all compile and KV-offload warmup steps
completed. The process printed the start of `test_5_concurrent_churn`, produced
no further progress, and was terminated by the timeout.

title: [TPU] Greedy output differs when a prompt is served from the prefix cache vs cold
body:
Greedy output changes when a prompt is served from the prefix cache instead of cold. Same prompt, `temperature: 0.0`, single host, no P/D, no HiCache.

```
run0 cached=0     ' The animal mentioned first in passage 0 is the fox.\n\nQuestion 1: ...'
run1 cached=1920  " \n\nOkay, let's see. The user provided a passage that's repeated multiple times. ..."
run2 cached=1920  " \n\nOkay, let's see. ..."   (identical to run1)
run3 cached=1920  " \n\nOkay, let's see. ..."   (identical to run1)
```

Deterministic: every cached run agrees with the other cached runs and differs from cold.
Also reproduces on a prompt with an unambiguous continuation (diverges mid-sequence rather
than at token 0), so it is not limited to near-tied logits.

Repro — `/weights/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`, one v7x host (4 chips / 8 cores):

```
MODEL=/weights/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP_SIZE=8 EP_SIZE=8 PAGE_SIZE=64 \
MEM_FRACTION_STATIC=0.30 QUANTIZATION= KV_CACHE_DTYPE= DISABLE_RADIX_CACHE=0 \
EXTRA_ARGS="--moe-runner-backend triton --max-total-tokens 16384 --enable-cache-report" \
bash benchmark/tpu/launch_server.sh
```

Then POST the same prompt (>= 1 page of shared prefix) to `/generate` twice with
`temperature: 0.0` and compare `text`. `meta_info.cached_tokens` confirms the second
request hit the cache. `DISABLE_RADIX_CACHE=0` is required — the launcher defaults it to
`1`. `--moe-runner-backend triton` is only to work around #317.

Observed matrix (4 identical requests per cell; run0 cold, runs 1-3 cache hits):

| config | repetitive prompt | unambiguous prompt |
|---|---|---|
| `--disable-radix-cache` | 4/4 identical | 3/4 identical (1 sporadic outlier) |
| radix cache on, `pallas_tpu_rpa_v3` | cold != cached | cold != cached |
| radix cache on, `pallas_tpu_rpa_batched` | 4/4 identical | cold != cached |
| radix cache on, `--tpu-compile-tokens 2048` (single token bucket) | cold != cached | cold != cached |
| radix cache on, `--chunked-prefill-size 512` | cold != cached (both outputs swap vs the unchunked row) | 4/4 identical |

Ruled out by the above:

- HiCache / KV offload — reproduces with the radix cache alone.
- P/D disaggregation — reproduces single-host.
- TP size — also seen at TP4.
- Sampling — `temperature: 0.0`.
- Attention backend version — both RPA backends affected.
- Token-bucket / block-size differences between the 1941-token cold prefill and the
  21-token extend — pinning both to one bucket does not fix it.

title: TPU CI stage-a: test_qwen3_vl_tpu_compile_annotation fails with 'duplicate name: dynamo_minifier_backend' on current main
body:
The TPU unit stage fails on `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_vl_tpu_compile_annotation.py::test_tpu_platform_selects_tpu_vision_backend` with:

```
File "torch/_dynamo/repro/after_dynamo.py", line 316, in <module>
File "torch/_dynamo/backends/registry.py", line 105, in register_backend
  assert name not in _COMPILER_FNS, f"duplicate name: {name}"
AssertionError: duplicate name: dynamo_minifier_backend
```

The trigger chain is the module-scope `torch.compile` at `srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py:66`, reached during model import; under torch_tpu's patched `torch.compile` (`torch_tpu/_loader.py:85`) it resolves the compiler eagerly, which imports `torch._dynamo.repro.after_dynamo` a second time in the same process and trips torch's backend-registry duplicate assert.

Evidence this is main-branch, not PR-specific:
- Reproduces on a clean `main` checkout (`fd586db8b`) on a TPU host: `python3 test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_vl_tpu_compile_annotation.py -f` → same assert. Also reproduces at `d6291fecf` and its parent, so it predates the recent MoE change.
- In CI it is intermittent across pods: passed on `praj/tpu-rpa-long-context-smem` (same merge-base `fd586db8b`) at 20:15Z, failed on PR #273 in three completed attempts (latest 22:27Z).

Currently blocks any PR that runs the TPU stage. Happy to help validate a fix; a candidate direction is making the `deep_gemm.py` module-scope compile lazy, or guarding the duplicate registration.

title: [TPU] Unit test crash: duplicate torch-dynamo backend 'dynamo_minifier_backend'
body:
## Summary

The registered unit test
[`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_vl_tpu_compile_annotation.py`](test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_vl_tpu_compile_annotation.py)
errors on import when run through the TPU unit suite:

```
assert name not in _COMPILER_FNS, f"duplicate name: {name}"
AssertionError: duplicate name: dynamo_minifier_backend
ERROR: test_tpu_platform_selects_tpu_vision_backend (TestQwen3VLTpuCompileAnnotation)
```

## Root cause

Importing the test's dependencies — `sglang.srt.compilation.support_torch_compile`
and/or `sglang.srt.platforms` — registers the torch-dynamo backend
`dynamo_minifier_backend` a second time, and `torch._dynamo.backends.registry`
rejects the duplicate (`_COMPILER_FNS` name collision). The registration is not
idempotent / a module gets imported twice along different paths.

## Repro

On a TPU host (or any host where the import chain runs):

```
python3 test/run_suite.py --hw tpu --suite stage-a-test-tpu-unit
```

The run dies ~2 min in on this file. NOTE: because the run stops at the first failing
file, the status of the remaining ~29 unit tests is currently unknown — they should be
re-checked once this is fixed (a "continue past failures" pass would enumerate them).

## Why it appeared now

The test file was added recently (#195, 2026-07-22) and had never been exercised through
a CI gate until the TPU PR gate started running the registered tree end-to-end.

## Impact

Blocks the TPU unit suite (`stage-a-test-tpu-unit`) at collection/import of this file.
**CI infra is unaffected** — the gate correctly caught this.

## Possible fixes (for discussion)

- Make the dynamo backend registration idempotent (guard against re-register), or
- Fix the double-import path in `support_torch_compile` / `platforms`, or
- Adjust the test's imports so it doesn't trigger a second registration.

title: [TPU] Serving crashes at startup: TpuDeviceModule has no attribute 'graph_pool_handle'
body:
## Summary

Launching an SGLang server on TPU with `--enable-torch-compile` crashes at startup during CUDA-graph init:

```
AttributeError: type object 'TpuDeviceModule' has no attribute 'graph_pool_handle'
```

The scheduler dies before serving any request.

## Call chain

```
scheduler.run_scheduler_process → Scheduler.__init__ → init_model_worker
  → init_all_cuda_graphs → tp_worker.init_cuda_graphs
  → model_runner.init_cuda_graphs → init_prefill_cuda_graph
  → PrefillCudaGraphRunner.__init__ → resolve_prefill_backend
  → TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend.__init__ → _run_compile_pass
  → runner_utils/pool.py:39  resources.graph_memory_pool = device_module.graph_pool_handle()
  → AttributeError
```

## Root cause

`--enable-torch-compile` routes prefill through `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend`, whose
`get_or_create_global_graph_memory_pool` calls `device_module.graph_pool_handle()` — a
CUDA-only API that `TpuDeviceModule` does not implement.

The TPU platform *does* try to opt out — [`tpu_platform.py`](python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/tpu_platform.py) sets
`disable_cuda_graph=True` and `disable_piecewise_cuda_graph=True` — but the newer
torch-compile prefill cuda-graph path bypasses those guards and runs anyway.

## Why it appeared now

This surfaced the first time the CI gate built the image from `main`-rebased code and
ran the serving suite on TPU. The relevant upstream changes are recent:
- prefill cuda-graph runner (#27988, 2026-07-06)
- cuda graph enabled by default (#29458, 2026-07-01)
- shared prefill/decode graph memory pool (#28973, 2026-06-24)

Earlier TPU serving validation used a pre-rebase image without this path.

## Repro

Run the serving suite on a TPU host:

```
python3 test/run_suite.py --hw tpu --suite stage-b-test-tpu-4-v7
```

Both `test_tpu_basic_inference` and `test_prefix_cache` fail (server crashes at
startup). Both launch with `--enable-torch-compile`.

## Impact

All TPU serving (`stage-b-test-tpu-*`) with torch-compile enabled. Blocks the serving
suite in the nightly TPU gate. **CI infra is unaffected** — the gate correctly caught this.

## Possible fixes (for discussion)

- Make the prefill cuda-graph / `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend` path respect
  `disable_(piecewise_)cuda_graph` on TPU (skip it), or
- Provide a `graph_pool_handle()` shim on `TpuDeviceModule`, or
- Force `--disable-cuda-graph` for TPU serving launches until the path is TPU-aware.

title: [RFC] CI/CD
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

# sglang-torchtpu CI/CD Proposal

**Scope:** Private fork (`sglang-torchtpu`) — period before upstream merge to `sgl-project/sglang`.

---

## TL;DR

### Work and Resource Required

| Bucket | What we need to build | Owner / dependency |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Hardware** | TPU v7 quota in our GCP project. Recommended pool: \~4× single-chip v7 runners (PR unit), 1× 4-chip v7 runner (PR suite), 1× 4-chip v7 runner (nightly \+ perf). | GCP project \+ TPU v7 quota (already have both). |
| **Runner infra** | Stand up Actions Runner Controller (ARC) on a GKE cluster in the same project; add TPU v7 node pools (`tpu7x-...`); register runner scale sets with labels `tpu-v7-1`, `tpu-v7-4`. | One-time GKE config; ongoing GCE/TPU spend. |
| **Container image** | Build `docker/tpu.Dockerfile` once, publish to **private GAR**. Pinned torch \+ `torch_tpu` wheel \+ `libtpu` \+ `jax[tpu]`. Rebuilt nightly and on Dockerfile/dep changes. | GAR repo \+ workload-identity binding. |
| **`torch_tpu` wheel access** | Wheel is published to a **private package server**. CI containers and dev machines need read auth. Plan: workload-identity (GKE→GAR) for CI; short-lived OAuth token mounted at install time. No long-lived secrets. | Permission grant on the private wheel server. |
| **Workflows** | `pr-test-tpu.yml` (gate → check-changes → 3 TPU stages → CUDA guard → finish), `release-docker-tpu.yml` (image build/push), `nightly-test-tpu.yml` (full suite \+ perf trend), `rebase-from-upstream.yml` (twice-weekly rebase). | All additive — no edits to existing CUDA/NPU/AMD workflows. |
| **Test harness** | Add `HWBackend.TPU` \+ `register_tpu_ci()` to the existing registry, add TPU suite names to [test/run\_suite.py](http://test/run_suite.py), promote `test/manual/tpu/` to `test/registered/tpu/`. | None — code-only. |
| **Branch protection** | Required checks: `lint`, `pr-gate`, `pr-test-tpu-finish`, `stage-cuda-guard` (from day 1). | GitHub repo settings. |
| **GPU resource** | 1× shared L4 (or cheapest CUDA runner) for the mandatory CUDA guard job. Existing upstream-sized runners not required. | Modest — non-TPU spend. |

---

## 1\. Context and goals

`sglang-torchtpu` is a temporary private fork of sglang that adds a TPU backend. The fork will be developed for some number of weeks, then merged back into `sgl-project/sglang`.

During this period we want:

- **High signal CI on TPU.** Every PR must run a fast TPU unit (≤15 min) on real hardware before merge — mocking the TPU defeats the purpose of the fork.  
- **No regressions on the other backends we ship from this fork.** The TPU work edits shared files ([parallel\_state.py](http://python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py), [utils/common.py](http://python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py), [scheduler.py](http://python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py), [attention\_registry.py](http://python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py)). A green TPU build that breaks CUDA is not acceptable when we merge upstream.  
- **A clean merge story.** CI in this fork should look like a strict subset/superset of upstream sglang CI — adding `register_tpu_ci` and a `pr-test-tpu.yml` workflow that upstream can adopt verbatim, with no other invasive changes to the test harness.  
- **Cheap to run.** TPU VMs are expensive. We must gate, partition, and batch carefully.

Non-goals during the fork window: matching upstream's full NVIDIA matrix (B200/H200/H20/GB200), running nightlies on every accelerator, releasing wheels to PyPI.

---

## 2\. High-level architecture

### 2.1 Pipeline shape

```
                       ┌──────────────────────────┐
   pull_request ─────► │ pr-gate (cheap, fast)    │
                       │  - lint / pre-commit     │
                       │  - run-ci label gate     │
                       │  - cool-down rate limit  │
                       └─────────────┬────────────┘
                                     │ pass
                                     ▼
                       ┌──────────────────────────┐
                       │ check-changes            │
                       │  - dorny/paths-filter    │
                       │  - main_package / tpu /  │
                       │    sgl-kernel / docs     │
                       └─────────────┬────────────┘
                                     │ fan-out
              ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
              ▼                      ▼                      ▼
   stage-tpu-unit-1chip   stage-tpu-tp4-v7         stage-cuda-guard
   (v7 1-chip, ~10 min)    (v7 4-chip, ~30 min)     (1×L4, single-GPU
   PR-blocking             PR-blocking on tpu/      smoke; MANDATORY
                           backend changes          from day 1)
              │                      │                      │
              └──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┘
                                     ▼
                       ┌──────────────────────────┐
                       │ pr-test-tpu-finish       │
                       │  aggregate + report      │
                       └──────────────────────────┘

   schedule (nightly)  ─► nightly-test-tpu.yml      (v7 tp4 + perf)
   schedule (2×/week)  ─► rebase-from-upstream.yml  (open PR from upstream main)
   release tag         ─► release-docker-tpu.yml    (build & push GAR image)
```

Each box is a separate workflow file. Required GitHub checks point at `pr-test-tpu-finish` and `pr-gate` only — keeping the required-set small avoids re-running unrelated nightlies whenever GitHub demands a re-run.

Pattern source: this mirrors [.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml](http://.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml) (stage-based NPU pipeline with a `pr-test-npu-finish` aggregator) and [.github/workflows/pr-test-xpu.yml](http://.github/workflows/pr-test-xpu.yml) (single docker-build-then-test job).

### 2.2 Where TPU tests live

We extend the existing test-discovery system rather than inventing a parallel one:

| Concern | Existing mechanism we reuse |
| :---- | :---- |
| Backend enum | [ci\_register.py](http://python/sglang/test/ci/ci_register.py) `HWBackend` — add `TPU` and `register_tpu_ci()` |
| Suite catalog | [test/run\_suite.py](http://test/run_suite.py) — add `HWBackend.TPU` keys to `PER_COMMIT_SUITES` / `NIGHTLY_SUITES` |
| Test runner | `python3 test/run_suite.py --hw tpu --suite <name>` |
| Partitioning | `--auto-partition-id` \+ `--auto-partition-size` (already supports any backend) |
| Test home | `test/registered/tpu/` mirroring `test/registered/ascend/` layout |

The TPU unit tests that currently live at [test/manual/tpu/](http://test/manual/tpu/) get **promoted to** `test/registered/tpu/basic_function/` and gain `register_tpu_ci(...)` markers. `test/manual/tpu/` is then deleted — manual-only tests rot fast.

The upstream merge story is then: one self-contained PR that adds `HWBackend.TPU`, the registry, the suite entries, and `test/registered/tpu/`. The workflow file (`pr-test-tpu.yml`) is appended; no upstream workflow files need to change.

### 2.3 Runner topology

Self-hosted GKE runner pool with TPU v7 node groups. We run [Actions Runner Controller (ARC)](https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller) on GKE inside our GCP project. TPU v7 node pools back two runner scale sets:

| Label | Node pool | Used by | Capacity target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `tpu-v7-1` | single-chip v7 | `stage-a-test-tpu-unit` | 2–4 concurrent (matches expected PR rate) |
| `tpu-v7-4` | 4-chip v7 (1 host) | `stage-b-test-tpu-4-v7`, `nightly-tpu-4-v7`, `nightly-perf-tpu` | 1 PR slot \+ 1 nightly slot |

Mapping basis: `tp_size ∈ {1, 8}` covers the paths `_prepare_tpu_env` and [allocator\_tpu.py](http://python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/allocator_tpu.py) exercise. Same shape as `torch_tpu`'s v7 runner label `linux-x86-tpu7x-224-4tpu` ([torch\_tpu/.github/workflows/postsubmit.yml](http://../../torch_tpu/.github/workflows/postsubmit.yml)).

References:

- Google's ARC \+ TPU writeup: [https://cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/tutorials/run-github-actions-on-tpu](https://cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/tutorials/run-github-actions-on-tpu)  
- ARC: [https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller](https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller)  
- TPU v7 system architecture: [https://cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/system-architecture-tpu-vm](https://cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/system-architecture-tpu-vm)

### 2.4 Container strategy

Two layers, with two corresponding workflows. Same split as upstream sglang ([docker/npu.Dockerfile](http://docker/npu.Dockerfile) \+ [release-docker-npu.yml](http://.github/workflows/release-docker-npu.yml)):

1. **Base image** — `docker/tpu.Dockerfile`. Pinned `torch==2.10.0`, `torch_tpu==<commit>`, `libtpu`, `jax` (for pallas), plus our normal sglang runtime deps. Built nightly \+ on changes to the Dockerfile or `python/pyproject_tpu.toml`. Tagged `:nightly`, `:<sha>`, `:vX.Y.Z`. Pushed to **private** Google Artifact Registry (GAR) inside the same GCP project as the runners — no DockerHub egress, no rate limits, no public exposure.  
     
2. **CI image** — same Dockerfile, but the test job mounts the PR's source via `actions/checkout` and reinstalls sglang in-place. This is how XPU does it ([.github/workflows/pr-test-xpu.yml](http://.github/workflows/pr-test-xpu.yml) lines 82–117): build once, run container, `docker exec` to install and test.

A "build wheel in stage-a, consume in stage-b" pattern (what CUDA does for `sgl-kernel/` via `sgl-kernel-build-wheels`) is **not** needed initially — there are no TPU-specific C++/CUDA kernels in this fork yet. Revisit if/when we add custom Pallas or XLA kernels with their own build step.

### 2.4a `torch_tpu` wheel access (private package server)

The `torch_tpu` wheel is published to a private package server (not PyPI, not a public GAR). Both the Dockerfile build and the CI test jobs must authenticate to read it. We do **not** want long-lived passwords baked into images or stored as plain GitHub secrets.

**Auth model:**

- **CI jobs (GKE-hosted runners) → wheel server:** use workload identity. Each runner pod assumes a GCP service account (`tpu-ci-reader@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) that has read-only IAM on the wheel server (if it's GAR-backed) or a short-lived OAuth2 token (if it's a custom Artifactory/PyPI server backed by IAP). The token is fetched by `gcloud auth print-access-token` at install time and passed to `pip` via `--index-url https://oauth2accesstoken:${TOKEN}@<host>/<repo>/simple/`.  
- **Docker image build → wheel server:** the build runs on a GKE-hosted runner too (not ubuntu-latest), so the same workload-identity path applies. The Dockerfile takes a `--build-arg PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL=...` injected by the workflow, and **never** persists the token into a layer (use a multi-stage build or `RUN --mount=type=secret`).  
- **Local dev machines → wheel server:** developers run `gcloud auth application-default login` once; the install scripts (e.g. `scripts/ci/tpu/tpu_ci_install_dependency.sh`) call `gcloud auth print-access-token` the same way. No `.netrc`, no checked-in tokens.

**Token lifetime:** OAuth tokens are 1-hour. CI jobs renew at install time only; jobs longer than 1 hour are fine because the wheel is downloaded in the first minute. Document this in `scripts/ci/tpu/tpu_ci_install_dependency.sh` so a future debugger doesn't burn time on "401 after 1 hour" symptoms.

**Failure mode to handle in CI:** if the wheel server is briefly unreachable, the install retries 3× with exponential backoff before failing the job. Don't let one network blip burn a 4-chip v7 runner-hour.

Reference patterns:

- `google-github-actions/auth@v2` workload-identity setup: [https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth](https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth)  
- `pip` index URL with bearer auth: [https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/authentication/](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/authentication/)

### 2.5 Cost and gating discipline

- **`paths-filter` is mandatory.** Following [pr-test-npu.yml](http://.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml) lines 60–73, the `check-changes` job filters on `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/**`, `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/pallas*`, `test/registered/tpu/**`, `docker/tpu.Dockerfile`, `python/pyproject_tpu.toml`, `scripts/ci/tpu/**`, `.github/workflows/pr-test-tpu.yml`. Docs-only and unrelated-backend PRs skip TPU entirely.  
- **`run-ci` label requirement** stays on (inherited from [pr-gate.yml](http://.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml)). For low-permission contributors this also enforces a cool-down so a PR rebase storm cannot burn TPU hours.  
- **`cancel-in-progress` per branch.** Forces serial runs per PR.  
- **Auto-partition** suites that exceed \~30 min so a single retry doesn't restart the whole suite.  
- **Cache HF models** on a persistent disk mounted into the runner (`/cache/hf`), same pattern as XPU's `-v $HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface`.  
- **Test budget per PR:** target ≤45 chip-minutes (1 chip × 15 min unit \+ 4 chip × \~8 min suite). Anything beyond moves to nightly.

### 2.6 Branch protection

    2. `git fetch upstream main`.  
    3. Create a throwaway branch `bot/rebase-upstream-<date>` from our `main`.  
    4. Attempt `git merge upstream/main --no-ff`.  
    5. **On clean merge:** open a PR from `bot/rebase-upstream-<date>` → `main`. Title: `[rebase] Pull upstream sglang main (<short-sha>)`. Labels: `run-ci`, `auto-rebase`. The full TPU \+ CUDA-guard CI runs against it — if green, a human merges (1 approving review still required).  
    6. **On merge conflicts:** do **not** open a PR. Instead, open a GitHub issue titled `[rebase] Manual conflict resolution needed (<short-sha>)` with a code-block listing the conflicted paths and a copy-pasteable `git fetch && git merge` command. Assign to the on-call TPU dev (rotation tracked in `.github/CODEOWNERS`).

28. Keep a 1-line entry in `MERGE_PLAN.md` for each rebase PR (date \+ upstream sha range) so the eventual upstream-merge-back PR can trace which sync windows the TPU changes survived.

Operational note: do not run rebase while a nightly is in flight. The workflow's `concurrency` group should be `rebase-from-upstream` with `cancel-in-progress: false` so two rebase attempts queue rather than collide.
